title: [Varicocele: comparison of minimally invasive treatment options : Endovascular embolization, microsurgery, and patient-tailored treatment selection].
abstract: BACKGROUND: Varicocele is the most common potentially treatable cause of male subfertility. Endovascular embolization is an established minimally invasive alternative to microsurgical ligation. OBJECTIVE: To place the indications, technique, outcomes, and limitations of varicocele embolization in context and to define its role relative to microsurgery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Narrative, guideline- and evidence-based review of current WHO, EAU, AUA/ASRM, and CIRSE recommendations, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant cohort studies published through July 2026. RESULTS: Treatment is primarily indicated in men with a palpable varicocele, abnormal semen parameters, and otherwise unexplained infertility; subclinical varicoceles and normal semen analyses do not justify intervention. Technical success of embolization is usually above 90% in experienced centers. Pregnancy rates are broadly similar to those after surgery, while overall morbidity tends to be lower. Recurrence may, however, be more frequent than after high ligation. No embolic agent has proved consistently superior. CONCLUSION: Varicocele embolization is an evidence-based alternative to surgery, particularly for recurrent disease, bilateral or complex venous anatomy, and when rapid recovery is a priority. Treatment should be selected through multidisciplinary, anatomy-based, and shared decision-making.

Endovascular embolization is an established minimally invasive alternative to microsurgical ligation. OBJECTIVE: To place the indications, technique, outcomes, and limitations of varicocele embolization in context and to define its role relative to microsurgery.

title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 2 After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I= 0%; t= 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I= 0%; t= 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I= 0%; τ= 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1). METHODS: Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Automated Detection of Endoleaks in CT Angiography Using a Single Deep Learning Model.
abstract: AIM: Detecting endoleaks on post-EVAR CT scans, especially in the presence of artifacts caused by embolic agents like Onyx, is a challenging but critical task. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based method for endoleak detection using a single object detection model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective dataset comprising 249 CT scans was used, divided into training (129 scans) and test (120 scans) datasets. Ground truth annotations were obtained through 3D manual segmentation, and a preprocessing pipeline was applied. The model was trained on slices extracted from the training dataset and validated using standard metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, and AUC. RESULTS: The model achieved high performance at both the per-slice and per-series levels. Per-slice detection yielded a ROC AUC of 96%, with a sensitivity of 91%, specificity of 93%, PPV of 55%, and NPV of 99%. At the per-series level, sensitivity and specificity were 93% and 95%, respectively. Notably, our method introduces a per-slice detection metric, which was not reported in previous studies, and uses a single model, making it computationally efficient and easy to train. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for endoleak detection, offering a robust and efficient tool for clinical practice. Future work could focus on expanding the dataset and integrating additional predictive capabilities, such as endoleak classification and localization.

In this study, we propose a deep learning-based method for endoleak detection using a single object detection model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective dataset comprising 249 CT scans was used, divided into training (129 scans) and test (120 scans) datasets.

title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biologic stent-graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for type 1 diabetes mellitus. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22 μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQ]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQ) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by ELISA. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling under idealized, non-physiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries. RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 ± 8 vs. 145 ± 20 μIU/mL under low vs. high glucose (p = 0.02), and secretion rates were 5,344 ± 144 vs. 6,795 ± 503 μIU/hr (p = 0.008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 ± 13 vs. 300 ± 17 μIU/mL (p = 0.014). CONCLUSION: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent-graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

title: Minimally invasive Ayurveda management of recurrent and acute-on-chronic non-healing venous leg ulceration - a Case Report.
abstract: Slow healing and recurrent venous leg ulcers resulting from varicose veins due to lower limb chronic venous insufficiency are common vascular complications. If left untreated, they may lead to severe outcomes such as hemorrhage and, in extreme cases, limb amputation. We report the case of a 61-year-old male with bilateral lower limb varicosities of 10 years' duration, presenting with multiple painful venous leg ulcers that recurred several months after phlebectomy due to patient non-compliance. Physical examination revealed exquisitely tender, exudative, irregular-bordered, multiple shallow ulcers with sloping edges and a putrid odor. The surrounding tissue was oedematous and indurated, predominantly involving the areas in and around the ankle joints. Aerobic wound swab culture showed heavy growth of Klebsiella pneumoniae and Proteus hauseri, with moderate growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. One month of Ayurvedic intervention employing vrana sodhana and vrana ropana cikitsa resulted in accelerated wound healing in recurrent, acute-on-chronic, non-healing venous leg ulcerations.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: p At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants.In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions. METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years. RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used. CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

title: The Importance of Family Centered Care and Cascade Screening in Patients with Heritable Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm diseases (HTAAD) may be either syndromic or non-syndromic. While family screening for all forms of HTAAD has been recommended, providing care to an entire family is often fragmented in our siloed healthcare delivery model. We sought to determine the frequency of cascade family screening in the current era with either cardiovascular imaging (cascade cardiac screening) and/or genetic testing (cascade genetic screening), and to assess the impact of such testing on adverse outcomes in first degree family members. Of the 184 HTAAD patients who presented to our academic center without a known family history of aneurysmal disease, 84 were followed in a cardiology clinic, 40 in a genetics clinic and 60 in a combined cardiovascular genetics clinic for both children and adults. Cascade cardiac or genetic screening of ≥ 1 family member occurred during the course of care in 138 of 184 (75%) families. Complete cascade screening (genetic and/or cardiac) of all at-risk first-degree family members occurred in only 61 (33%) families and varied by clinic type (12%, 10% and 78%, p = 0.001) for those initially evaluated in a cardiology, genetics, or combined cardiovascular genetics clinic. As a result of cascade screening or an aortic event, 461 additional family members were identified as at risk for an aortic event. Of these, 53 family members from 42 families experienced an unexpected HTAAD-related event. Cascade screening was associated with a lower incidence of an event (1/53 vs. 52/53, p < 0.0001) during follow-up. Clinics that offer family-based care and on-site cascade screening facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention thereby reducing mortality from aortic disease.

title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.

title: Labetalol-induced hyperkalemia in acute aortic dissection: A rare but clinically relevant adverse effect.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia is a potentially life-threatening electrolyte abnormality often associated with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, renal dysfunction, or potassium-sparing agents. Non-selective beta-blockers, including labetalol, may also precipitate hyperkalemia through beta-2 (β-2)-adrenergic blockade, although this adverse effect is underrecognized, particularly in patients without underlying renal disease. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, asthma, and polysubstance use disorder presented with severe chest pain and hypertensive emergency (243/132 mmHg). Imaging revealed aortic dilatation and confirmed acute type B aortic dissection. After initial medical management with intravenous (IV) esmolol and nicardipine, oral labetalol was initiated and escalated to 600 mg for anti-impulse therapy. The patient developed persistent, non-hemolyzed hyperkalemia (5.2 to 5.8 mmol/L) temporally correlating with labetalol dose escalation, despite preserved renal function (serum creatinine 1.4 to 1.8 mg/dL) and absence of RAAS inhibitors or heparin exposure. Conservative management failed, and the patient underwent thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE). Post-operatively, labetalol was discontinued and replaced with carvedilol. Serum potassium (K+) normalized within 48 hours and remained without further K+ lowering agents. Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale assessment yielded a score of 7, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction. CONCLUSIONS: Labetalol may induce clinically significant hyperkalemia independent of renal impairment or typical precipitating medications. This case highlights the importance of monitoring K+ in patients receiving labetalol for acute aortic syndromes and supports carvedilol as a potentially safer non-selective beta-blocker alternative with respect to K+ homeostasis.

title: Association of chronic kidney disease with major cardiovascular outcomes following lower extremity endovascular revascularization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) amplifies cardiovascular risk, yet its stage-specific influence on perioperative outcomes following endovascular lower extremity revascularization (LER) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the ACS NSQIP registry (2013-2022). Adults undergoing endovascular LER for PAD were stratified by preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) via the CKD-EPI 2021 equation: G1 (≥90), G2 (60-89), G3 (30-59), G4 (15-29), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis dependent). The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: myocardial infarction, stroke, or death). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Among 22,424 patients (64.6% aged ≥65 years; 36.1% women), comorbidity burden increased progressively with CKD stage. Within 30 days, 556 patients (2.5%) experienced MACE. Event rates rose stepwise: 1.5% (G1), 1.6% (G2), 2.7% (G3), 4.9% (G4), and 6.0% (G5). After adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, ASA class, admission status, presenting symptoms, and preoperative hematocrit, advanced CKD remained independently associated with MACE: OR 2.30 (95% CI 1.50-3.52) for G4 and OR 3.15 (95% CI 2.28-4.35) for G5 versus G1. CONCLUSION: CKD stage provides independent prognostic information in patients undergoing endovascular LER. Advanced CKD independently predicts 30-day MACE with a dose-response relationship across stages. Preoperative eGFR should be incorporated into perioperative risk stratification protocols to guide cardiovascular optimization and surveillance planning.

title: Structures and functions of enzymes involved in primary and secondary metabolite biosynthesis mediated by amino-group carrier protein.
abstract: Thermus thermophilus, an extremely thermophilic bacterium, synthesizes lysine through a novel type of 2-aminoadipate (AAA) pathway. The pathway starts from the synthesis of homocitrate using 2-oxoglutarate and acetyl-CoA. Homocitrate is converted to 2-oxoadipate by sequential reactions similar to the corresponding reactions in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. AAA formed by the transamination of 2-oxoadipate is loaded on amino-group carrier protein (AmCP) via isopeptide bond linkage. AAA is successively converted to lysine on AmCP by several reactions, and lysine is finally released from the carrier protein. A similar AmCP-mediated system is found in lysine and ornithine/arginine biosyntheses of archaea. Furthermore, the AmCP-mediated system is diversified in secondary metabolite biosynthesis with some modifications in various bacteria, including Streptomyces. This review shares the AmCP-mediated biosynthesis system and its contribution to expanding the structural diversity of natural compounds, along with the evolutionary aspects of lysine and arginine biosyntheses.

title: Cerebral No-Reflow after Thrombectomy: International Delphi Consensus on Definition and Imaging Assessment.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The operational definition and imaging assessment of the no-reflow phenomenon, a potential contributor to poor clinical outcome despite successful thrombectomy, remains debated. We aimed to develop expert-based international consensus on the definition, assessment, and reporting standard of cerebral no-reflow post-thrombectomy. METHODS: Three-rounds of a modified Delphi web-based survey was conducted among corresponding authors of peer-reviewed clinical studies on cerebral no-reflow between 2020 and 2025. Responses at each round were used to develop structured questionnaires for subsequent rounds. Consensus was predefined as ≥65% agreement. RESULTS: Among 27 panelists, the response rate was 70%, 74%, and 74% over all rounds. There was broad agreement to conceptualize no-reflow as macrovascular recanalization with impaired microvascular reperfusion. Consensus was reached that macrovascular recanalization is ideally assessed as (1) digital subtraction angiography with expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) grades 2c without clear distal vessel occlusions and/or eTICI 3 only, and (2) absence of a wedge-shaped time-to-maximum (Tmax) or time-to-peak (TTP) delay on post-recanalization perfusion computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Regarding impaired microvascular reperfusion assessment, cerebral blood flow, and/or volume were preferred over time-based perfusion parameters (Tmax/TTP). The panel expressed a preference that no-reflow should ideally be assessed ≤6 hours post-recanalization. Pending formal validation, histopathological-radiological correlation in animal models would sufficiently validate the use of imaging-based definitions in humans. INTERPRETATION: Based on currently available literature and expert opinions, this Delphi study provides a framework for systematically reporting cerebral no-reflow after endovascular treatment (EVT). The variability in opinions regarding quantitative thresholds highlights priorities for future methodological standardization and validation studies. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Cardiometabolic Assessment in Patients with Overweight, Obesity, or Type 2 Diabetes Undergoing Artificial Intelligence-Based Retinal Screening: A Real-World Evidence Study.
abstract: Background: Methods: n n n Results: P P P P P Conclusions: Overweight, obesity, and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) increase the risk of vascular complications, including retinal vascular alterations. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based retinal screening enables early detection of microvascular damage, potentially contributing to appropriate cardiometabolic prevention strategies. We performed a realworld evidence observational study to assess cardiometabolic parameters as well as retinal vascular alterations using novel AI-based retinal imaging.Between September and December 2025, we recruited 301 consecutive adults with overweight,obesity, or T2DM; cardiometabolic assessment was performed, and all participants also underwent retinal screening with the Aireen AI system, distinguishing those who resulted positive (= 42), negative (= 204), or undetermined (= 55) at the screening.All patients who resulted positive at the screening were confirmed with a diagnosis of retinal alterations by the ophthalmologists. The presence of positive retinal screening (RS+) progressively increased with worsening fasting glycemia, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, carotid intima-media thickness, and endothelial function (< 0.001 for all). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed independent associations of RS+ with HbA1c [odds ratio (OR) 2.29,< 0.001], carotid stenosis (OR 1.06,< 0.001), fasting glucose (OR 1.02,< 0.001), and the triglyceride/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (OR 2.19,= 0.010).These findings suggest that AIbased retinal screening with advanced tools can effectively identify early microvascular damage in individuals with overweight, obesity, or T2DM, with RS+ prevalence reflecting glycemic burden and vascular dysfunction. Therefore, integrating AI retinal assessment into cardiometabolic prevention programs may enable timely interventions to prevent progression to vision-threatening complications and support comprehensive cardiovascular risk management.

title: Transforming value-based deep vein thrombosis care through a pharmacist-led clinic.
abstract: PURPOSE: To address gaps in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) care, our health system implemented a pharmacist-led DVT clinic to standardize treatment, provide immediate access to pharmacy and vascular surgery services, and reduce emergency department (ED) and inpatient utilization for DVT management. METHODS: This was a retrospective, pre-post cohort study of a DVT clinic that centralized imaging, diagnosis, anticoagulant initiation, and pharmacy services into a single outpatient location. Patients diagnosed with a DVT between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, were included. The co-primary outcomes were the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the acute care setting compared before and after the DVT clinic opened (2023 vs 2024) and compared between patients seen in the clinic or not (2024 only). A χ2 test was used to analyze the co-primary outcomes, with significance defined as a P value of less than 0.05. RESULTS: The pharmacist saw 205 patients across 363 visits in 2024. Compared to 2023 baseline data, the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the ED in 2024 decreased from 88.6% to 53.3% (P < 0.001), while the rate of inpatient admission for DVT decreased from 25.5% to 13.9% (P < 0.001). Stratified analysis of the 2024 data demonstrated significantly lower acute care utilization for DVT among patients managed in the DVT clinic compared to those not seen, including for ED encounters (15.2% vs 91.5%; P < 0.001) and inpatient admissions (1.8% vs 26%; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The pharmacist-led DVT clinic represents a transformative advancement in pharmacy practice, redefining the role of pharmacists in ambulatory care and establishing a replicable model to optimize value-based care that shifts treatment for appropriate populations from acute to outpatient management.

title: Peripheral venous access in the neonate: current evidence, persistent uncertainties, and proposal of a structured insertion bundle.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Peripheral venous access devices are the most frequently inserted invasive devices in neonatal intensive care, yet fewer than half of them complete the therapy for which they were placed, and their mean dwell time is between 32 and 36 h. Despite this, they have attracted far less attention than central venous access devices: insertion and maintenance practices remain heterogeneous, rarely neonate-specific, and almost never standardized. This narrative review examines the current evidence on indications, device choice, insertion technique, securement, surveillance, and complications of peripheral venous access in the newborn. Evidence suggests that polyurethane outperforms polytetrafluoroethylene; the largest available cohort study supports 26G as the default caliber, including for transfusion; cyanoacrylate securement, structured pre-procedural vein assessment, and dedicated vascular access teams are each associated with better outcomes. Much of this evidence, however, comes from retrospective single-center studies, and important questions-such as the potential advantages of integrated devices or of long peripheral catheters, the caliber-to-vein relationship, and objective detection of infiltration-remain open. CONCLUSION:  On this basis, we propose a protocol for Safe Insertion of Peripheral Venous Catheters (SIPVeC), a seven-step insertion bundle formatted the same way as the protocols already available for umbilical and central devices in the neonate. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Peripheral venous access devices are the most used vascular access device in neonates, yet most fail before therapy is completed. • Insertion and maintenance practices remain heterogeneous and are rarely neonate-specific. WHAT IS NEW: • Evidence now favors polyurethane, 26G devices, structured vein assessment, and cyanoacrylate securement. • The SIPVeC protocol translates these elements into a reproducible seven-step insertion bundle for peripheral devices in neonates.

This narrative review examines the current evidence on indications, device choice, insertion technique, securement, surveillance, and complications of peripheral venous access in the newborn.

title: Predictive Value of Intraoperative Transcranial Doppler Hemodynamic Monitoring for Cerebral Hyperperfusion Syndrome After Carotid Artery Stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (CHS) is a potentially serious complication following carotid artery stenting (CAS). Conventional risk assessment methods may not adequately capture rapid intraoperative hemodynamic changes. Real-time transcranial Doppler (TCD) monitoring may provide valuable information for the early identification of patients at risk of CHS. AIMS: To investigate the predictive value of intraoperative real-time hemodynamic monitoring using TCD ultrasonography for CHS following CAS. METHODS: A total of 600 patients who underwent CAS were included. Factors associated with CHS were analyzed, and the predictive performance and clinical utility of TCD parameters measured at the T1 time point were evaluated. RESULTS: Factors associated with CHS following CAS were identified. The combined use of TCD parameters at the T1 time point demonstrated high predictive value and substantial net clinical benefit. CONCLUSION: TCD parameters measured at the T1 time point may be useful for predicting CHS following CAS and guiding clinical decision-making.

title: Anticoagulation in cirrhosis: Indications, drug selection, and disease-modifying potential.
abstract: Anticoagulation in cirrhosis has evolved from a perceived contraindication to an integral component of modern liver disease management. Recognition of the fragile rebalanced hemostatic state has challenged the traditional concept of cirrhosis as an exclusively hemorrhagic disorder and provided the biological rationale for anticoagulation in selected patients. Beyond preventing thrombus extension and promoting portal vein recanalization, accumulating experimental and clinical evidence suggests that anticoagulants may exert disease-modifying effects by attenuating intrahepatic coagulation, hepatic fibrogenesis, sinusoidal dysfunction, and portal hypertension. The therapeutic landscape has also changed substantially. Direct oral anticoagulants have emerged as effective and generally safe alternatives to vitamin K antagonists and low-molecular-weight heparin in carefully selected patients, although important differences in pharmacokinetics, hepatic metabolism, renal elimination, and drug interactions require individualized anticoagulant selection. At the same time, management of portal vein thrombosis has shifted from a uniform treatment approach to a patient-centered strategy that considers thrombus characteristics, transplant candidacy, bleeding risk, and the increasing role of endovascular portal vein recanalization. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the indications for anticoagulation in cirrhosis, anticoagulant selection, management of portal vein thrombosis, and available clinical outcomes. It also examines the emerging concept of anticoagulation as a disease-modifying therapy and highlights key knowledge gaps that should guide future research. Together, these advances position anticoagulation as an increasingly important component of comprehensive cirrhosis care rather than a treatment reserved solely for thrombotic complications.

title: Venous thromboembolism after laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy with large myoma burden.
abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients undergoing myomectomy. To evaluate the impact of route of surgery, myoma burden, and operative time in the development of VTE in this population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (Canadian Task Force Classification II2) of targeted myomectomy data from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) SETTING: NSQIP Database PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Women aged ≥18 years undergoing laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy between 2011 and 2022. Patients were classified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes as having low or high myoma burden (>250 g or >4 fibroids). Patients undergoing hysterectomy, vaginal or hysteroscopic myomectomy, with malignant pathology, or missing operative time were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: Cases were identified by CPT codes. Variables including age, ethnicity, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, diabetes, hypertension, blood transfusion, inpatient status, and American Society of Anesthesiologists classification system scores were collected. Clinical predictors of VTE were evaluated by stratifying cases according to surgical route, operative time, year of procedure, and myoma burden. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 38,167 myomectomies occurring between 2011-2022 were included. Of these, 20,943 (54.9%) patients underwent laparotomy, and 17,224 (45.1%) patients underwent laparoscopy. The incidence of VTE after myomectomy was 0.28%. Patients undergoing laparotomy had twice the VTE rate (0.36%) compared with those undergoing laparoscopy (0.18%). Patients undergoing laparotomy were more likely to be younger, of non-Hispanic African American ethnicity, inpatient, with higher BMI, require blood transfusion, have higher myoma burden, and have shorter operative times. After multivariable adjustment, neither myoma burden nor surgical route was independently associated with VTE. However, longer operative time (>186 min, 75 percentile) was independently associated with increased odds of VTE (aOR 2.73; CI:1.52-4.90). CONCLUSION: The occurrence of VTE after laparoscopic and laparotomic myomectomy is uncommon. The rate of VTE is higher with longer operative times, but this outcome is not significantly associated with surgical route or myoma burden.

title: Cardiovascular health in transgender and gender diverse individuals: an expert opinion on gender-affirming hormone therapy, risk assessment and clinical management.
abstract: Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) individuals represent a growing population with specific cardiovascular health needs. Current cardiovascular prevention strategies are largely derived from cisgender populations and may not adequately account for the combined effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) and other determinants. This expert opinion summarizes current evidence regarding cardiovascular health in TGD individuals, focusing on the cardiovascular effects of GAHT, population-specific cardiovascular risk factors, practical approaches to cardiovascular risk assessment, and future research priorities. Available evidence indicates that GAHT is associated with changes in cardiometabolic risk factors, haemostasis, vascular function, and cardiac physiology. Feminizing GAHT is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, whereas masculinizing GAHT is associated with adverse lipid changes, erythrocytosis, and a potentially increased risk of major cardiovascular events. However, causal inference is limited by the predominance of observational studies, relatively young study populations, heterogeneous GAHT regimens, short follow-up, and the absence of randomized study evidence. Population-level cardiovascular disparities in TGD should not be attributed to GAHT alone and smoking, obesity, physical inactivity, minority stress, socioeconomic disadvantage, and unequal access to healthcare may independently or interactively influence cardiovascular risk. Current cardiovascular risk prediction tools have not been validated or calibrated in TGD populations and do not account for GAHT exposure or TGD-specific psychosocial and structural determinants. Cardiovascular risk assessment in TGD individuals should integrate conventional risk factors, transgender-related cardiovascular risk factors, and patient involvement regarding individual goals. A coordinated multidisciplinary approach may facilitate personalized cardiovascular prevention while supporting access to gender-affirming care. Future research should prioritize long-term prospective studies and development of risk prediction models tailored to TGD populations.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: n n This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp ( = 261) or MHCA ( = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: p p The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Unilateral eosinophilic fasciitis: a case report and review of the literature.
abstract: A 59-year-old Japanese man developed pruritus and swelling of the right dorsal foot after weeding his garden in a crouching position for approximately one hour. Over a period of five months, the swelling, as well as skin induration, progressed unilaterally from the right thigh to the lower leg and dorsal foot. Laboratory tests, including eosinophil fraction and inflammatory markers, were within normal limits, and computed tomography showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis or malignancy. A full-thickness biopsy including the fascia revealed marked fascial thickening with fibrosis of the subcutaneous connective tissue, and perivascular lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrates without conspicuous eosinophils, leading to a diagnosis of eosinophilic fasciitis. Oral prednisolone (30 mg/day) resulted in gradual improvement. To the best of our knowledge, 11 cases of unilateral eosinophilic fasciitis have been reported (three in Japan and eight outside Japan). Including the present case (total 12), six cases lacked peripheral blood eosinophilia, and seven lacked significant eosinophilic infiltration in tissue; five showed neither. Eosinophilic fasciitis should be considered even in the absence of eosinophilia; therefore, early full-thickness biopsy including the fascia is essential for accurate diagnosis.

title: External Iliac Arteriovenous Fistula Caused by Stab Wound.
abstract: Major abdominal arteriovenous fistula (AVF), including external iliac vessels, is a rare condition. If untreated long term, AVFs may cause venous hypertension and heart failure. We report the case of a 47-year-old man who stabbed his left lower abdomen. His vital signs were stable. Computed tomography revealed hemoperitoneum and a left external iliac AVF. Prior to laparotomy, endovascular repair of AVF was performed. Subsequent laparotomy was performed, and omental injury and a small bowel injury were repaired. Exploration of the retroperitoneal hematoma showed no bleeding from the external iliac vessels. The patient was discharged on day 6. In the management of retroperitoneal hematoma after penetrating trauma, laparotomy has been recommended. Among hemodynamically stable patients with stab wounds and traumatic external iliac AVF, endovascular intervention may be considered prior to laparotomy. Further investigations are required to reveal the long-term safety and durability of a covered stent for traumatic AVFs.

title: Cerebral Hemodynamic Changes in Older Adults With Cognitive Complaints According to the Presence of Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: As a systemic expression of atherosclerosis, peripheral artery disease (PAD) has the potential to alter cerebral hemodynamics in elderly individuals presenting with cognitive concerns. However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized. METHODS: We conducted a single-center longitudinal observational study enrolling 132 participants (21 controls, 39 mild cognitive impairment, 72 mild Alzheimer's disease). All participants underwent transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography, ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement, brain MRI, and cognitive assessments at baseline and follow-up (~13.45 months). PAD was defined as ABI < 0.90. Bilateral mean flow velocity (MFV), pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI) of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) were tracked longitudinally across both time points. RESULTS: p p PAD was identified in 13 participants (9.8%). Baseline TCD parameters, vascular risk factors, white matter lesions on brain MRI, and cognitive measures were comparable between groups. At follow-up, the PAD group showed significantly higher MCA MFV after age adjustment (left < 0.001; right = 0.005). MFV increased in the PAD group (left +16.45 cm/s) but decreased in the non-PAD group (left -3.37 cm/s), with a significant between-group difference. PI and RI did not change in either group. Cognitive and functional outcomes were similar across groups throughout the study. CONCLUSION: These findings identify PAD as a condition associated with progressive MCA MFV elevation in the context of preserved cognition, implying that subclinical cerebrovascular changes are detectable by TCD before overt clinical worsening. Future research involving larger cohorts and extended follow-up is required to determine whether such hemodynamic changes forecast eventual cognitive deterioration.

However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized. title: Hemostatic dysfunction and thrombotic risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder with clinically relevant vascular and thrombotic consequences. Beyond hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, MASLD is associated with disturbances in hemostatic regulation that may shift the overall balance toward thrombosis. The prothrombotic phenotype of MASLD arises from the interaction of metabolic dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endothelial injury, platelet hyperreactivity, increased procoagulant activity, reduced natural anticoagulant capacity, and impaired fibrinolysis. These abnormalities may be detectable at early disease stages and appear to evolve with progression to steatohepatitis, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Epidemiological and clinical studies associate MASLD with venous thromboembolism, portal vein thrombosis, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke, with population-based data indicating approximately 1.8-fold higher venous thromboembolism risk and 3.4-fold higher PVT risk. However, conventional coagulation tests do not adequately reflect the net hemostatic balance, while candidate biomarkers and global hemostatic assays remain insufficiently validated for routine risk stratification. Hemostatic dysfunction in MASLD, particularly hypercoagulability, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and platelet activation, represents a clinically relevant but still underrecognized component of the disease. Clinical management should integrate liver disease stage, cardiometabolic burden, conventional thrombotic risk factors, and bleeding or procedural risk. Routine antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy cannot currently be recommended solely on the basis of MASLD-related laboratory abnormalities.

Beyond hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, MASLD is associated with disturbances in hemostatic regulation that may shift the overall balance toward thrombosis. The prothrombotic phenotype of MASLD arises from the interaction of metabolic dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endothelial injury, platelet hyperreactivity, increased procoagulant activity, reduced natural anticoagulant capacity, and impaired fibrinolysis.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. RESULTS: P Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89];=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

title: COG5 Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and aVariant in Aortic Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. RESULTS: HLA-A HLA-DQA2 COG5 TPM4 Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 nearand rs9276409 within) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in thegene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. CONCLUSIONS: COG5 This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidatevariant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Optimizing management strategies for T4b esophageal cancer: the role of TEVAR in multimodal treatment approaches.
abstract: BACKGROUND: T4b esophageal cancer with aortic invasion remains a major therapeutic challenge because treatment-related tumor regression may precipitate aortoesophageal fistula formation and catastrophic hemorrhage. While chemoradiotherapy is the backbone of disease control, the role of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) as prophylaxis or bridge therapy within a multimodal treatment strategy is increasingly recognized. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the use of TEVAR in T4b esophageal cancer. Relevant clinical studies, reviews and guideline documents were evaluated qualitatively, with emphasis on treatment sequencing, bleeding prevention, resectability and oncologic outcomes. RESULTS: Available retrospective studies and systematic reviews suggest that elective TEVAR may reduce the risk of major bleeding complications and facilitate subsequent esophagectomy in selected patients. Elective TEVAR was associated with higher rates of subsequent esophageal resection and fewer complications than salvage TEVAR. Moreover, elective TEVAR followed by esophagectomy, ameliorates significantly patients survival. These findings support the potential role of elective TEVAR within multimodal treatment strategies, although the available evidence remains predominantly retrospective and is subject to selection bias and heterogeneity in patient selection and treatment. CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may represent a useful adjunct in the multimodal management of selected patients with T4b esophageal cancer and aortic involvement. In carefully selected patients, elective TEVAR may reduce the risk of catastrophic hemorrhage and facilitate subsequent curative-intent treatment, including conversion esophagectomy, although prospective evidence defining its optimal indications and timing remains lacking.

title: Development of best practice statements for anticoagulation in advanced kidney disease using the modified Delphi method.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with advanced kidney disease (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) are known to have an increased risk of venous thromboembolic events and increased likelihood of atrial fibrillation alongside an increased risk of bleeding. People with advanced kidney disease are often excluded from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of anticoagulants, leaving gaps in the evidence base and practice variation. This study aimed to achieve consensus on anticoagulant use in advanced kidney disease to inform national prescribing guidance. METHODS: A modified Delphi approach was used to achieve consensus on statements relating to anticoagulant use in advanced kidney disease. Three Delphi rounds were predefined, with two rounds of questionnaires followed by online discussion in round three. Panel members included UK experts from the fields of cardiology, nephrology and haematology, who were asked to rate 160 statements with appropriateness and consensus defined by RAND methodology. RESULTS: Twenty-one experts completed rounds one and two of the Delphi. For round three, 11 experts joined a Microsoft Teams discussion. Following round three, there were 72 statements with consensus agreement for inclusion in the guideline, including dose reduction recommendations for therapeutic light molecular weight heparin (LMWH), recommendation for off-label apixaban use in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, and trough anti-Xa level monitoring with therapeutic LMWH. Forty-two statements with consensus disagreement for exclusion and 27 with unequivocal consensus. These statements could be used to develop research recommendations. CONCLUSION: This study has led to consensus agreement on a number of statements relating to anticoagulant use in advanced kidney disease in the UK that can be used in national guidance.

title: Impact of Perioperative Buyang Huanwu-Based Traditional Chinese Medicine Intervention on Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism, Coagulation Markers and Systemic Inflammation: A Propensity Score-Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) evaluate, in a propensity-score-weighted retrospective cohort, the effectiveness and safety of a standardised perioperative Buyang Huanwu-based traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction combined with standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis on the 30-day incidence of symptomatic and asymptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE), (2) characterise the longitudinal trajectories of coagulation (D-dimer, fibrinogen) and inflammatory (C-reactive protein [CRP]) biomarkers and (3) quantify the net clinical benefit of this integrative approach. METHODS: n n We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1847 adult patients undergoing major general-surgical or gynaecological procedures between January 2020 and December 2024 at a tertiary integrative-medicine centre. Patients receiving a standardised perioperative TCM decoction based on the modified Buyang Huanwu Tang in addition to standard LMWH prophylaxis (= 892) were compared with patients receiving standard prophylaxis alone (= 955). The TCM decoction comprised seven herbal components dispensed at fixed daily doses (Huangqi, 60 g; Danggui, 9 g; Chishao, 6 g; Chuanxiong, 6 g; Honghua, 3 g; Taoren, 6 g; Dilong, 9 g) supplemented with 15 g of Danshen; granules were prepared as a single-batch good manufacturing practice-certified concentrated formulation, with the principal bioactive markers astragaloside IV, ferulic acid, paeoniflorin and salvianolic acid B quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography and required to fall within ±10% of the label content to ensure dose standardisation. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was 30-day VTE confirmed by duplex ultrasonography or computed tomography pulmonary angiography, with symptomatic and asymptomatic events recorded separately. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, length of stay, patient-reported pain and 90-day all-cause mortality. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyse longitudinal trajectories of D-dimer, fibrinogen and CRP measured at baseline and on postoperative days 1, 3 and 7. RESULTS: p p p p p After IPTW adjustment, TCM intervention was associated with significantly reduced 30-day VTE incidence (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.58, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.41-0.82,= 0.002), with consistent protection observed for both symptomatic VTE (HR: 0.55, 95% CI: 0.34-0.89) and ultrasound-detected asymptomatic distal deep-vein thrombosis (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.39-0.94). Landmark analysis revealed sustained protection during both hospitalisation (HR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.33-0.81) and the post-discharge period (HR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.42-0.93). Linear mixed-effects modelling demonstrated significant group-by-time interactions for D-dimer (< 0.001) and CRP (= 0.003), indicating accelerated biomarker clearance in the TCM group: 42% faster D-dimer resolution and 38% faster CRP normalisation than in controls. No significant difference was observed for major bleeding (2.1% vs 2.4%,= 0.68) or 90-day all-cause mortality (1.6% vs 2.0%,= 0.51). Decision-curve analysis confirmed superior net clinical benefit across the clinically relevant threshold-probability range. CONCLUSION: Perioperative Buyang Huanwu-based TCM combined with standard LMWH prophylaxis significantly reduces postoperative VTE risk - for both symptomatic and ultrasound-detected asymptomatic events - through accelerated resolution of coagulation and inflammatory cascades, without increasing bleeding or 90-day all-cause mortality. These findings support the integration of standardised TCM into enhanced-recovery-after-surgery protocols, particularly for moderate- to high-risk surgical patients in whom anticoagulation intensification may be contraindicated.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Standalone Endovascular Embolization for Growing Meningiomas: A Multicenter Study Protocol.
abstract: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth. The primary end point is tumor growth control at 180 days after treatment, defined as a stable or reduced tumor volume based on quantitative volumetric assessment of the contrast-enhancing portion on magnetic resonance imaging. The secondary end points include the tumor volume change rate, embolized vessels, embolic materials, embolization results and characteristics, procedure-related complications, perioperative complications, functional outcomes (Karnofsky Performance Status and modified Rankin Scale), changes in clinical symptoms, and the need for additional treatment. Exploratory analyses will also assess the association between intratumoral penetration of embolic material and treatment outcomes. Patient recruitment is ongoing, and the results will be reported upon completion of the study. This study represents a prospective attempt to evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization for meningiomas. If safe tumor growth control can be achieved, this study may provide preliminary evidence supporting standalone embolization as a potential less-invasive treatment strategy.

This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth.

title: Suspected Mesenteric Malperfusion in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection During Pregnancy: A Case Report and Review of Reperfusion-First Strategies.
abstract: Aortic dissection during pregnancy is rare but potentially catastrophic. Acute Type A aortic dissection generally requires urgent surgical repair. When visceral malperfusion is present, however, the optimal sequence of interventions may be complex, particularly when pregnancy and recent cesarean delivery increase operative risk. Endovascular reperfusion followed by delayed aortic repair has been proposed in selected patients, although evidence supporting this strategy in pregnancy remains limited. A 37-year-old woman at 31 weeks' gestation presented with chest and back pain. Initial CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) performed for suspected pulmonary embolism excluded pulmonary embolism but demonstrated marked aortic root dilatation measuring 6.7 × 5.4 cm. Before definitive aortic imaging could be obtained, she developed acute respiratory deterioration and fetal distress, prompting emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. Postoperatively, transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe aortic root and ascending aortic dilatation, severe aortic regurgitation, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and a dissection flap consistent with Type A aortic dissection. Because of concern for catastrophic hemorrhage associated with cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest shortly after cesarean delivery, definitive aortic repair was deferred for approximately 24 h while the patient underwent medical optimization. During this interval, she developed progressive metabolic acidosis and worsening renal function, raising clinical concern for visceral malperfusion. Dedicated abdominal vascular imaging was not obtained, and therefore the presence, distribution, and mechanism of mesenteric malperfusion could not be anatomically confirmed before surgery. At subsequent operative exploration, extensive small- and large-bowel necrosis and markedly hypoperfused adnexal tissue were identified, precluding definitive aortic repair. The patient subsequently died after transition to comfort-focused care. In an analysis from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection, mesenteric malperfusion was associated with higher in-hospital mortality than dissection without malperfusion. This case highlights the diagnostic and management challenges of acute Type A aortic dissection during pregnancy. In a pregnant patient presenting with chest or back pain and marked aortic root dilatation on PE-protocol imaging, acute aortic syndrome should prompt urgent evaluation of the entire aorta. Progressive metabolic acidosis, renal dysfunction, or unexplained clinical deterioration should raise concern for visceral ischemia. Although reperfusion-first strategies have been described in selected patients with aortic dissection and mesenteric malperfusion, their applicability in pregnancy remains uncertain and depends on defined vascular anatomy and the mechanism of malperfusion.
englishSummary: Aortic dissection during pregnancy is rare but potentially catastrophic. Acute Type A aortic dissection generally requires urgent surgical repair. When visceral malperfusion is present, however, the optimal sequence of interventions may be complex, particularly when pregnancy and recent cesarean delivery increase operative risk.

title: Neuromonitoring of perioperative microembolization and its association with postoperative stroke after carotid endarterectomy.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to assess whether perioperative microembolization can identify patients at risk for postoperative stroke. METHODS: A total of 257 carotid endarterectomy procedures in 254 patients were analyzed (154 symptomatic, 103 asymptomatic). Neuromonitoring, combining transcranial Doppler ultrasonography and continuous electroencephalography, was utilized to evaluate cerebral perfusion and detect microembolic signals (MES). Monitoring covered the entire intraoperative phase and a standardized 20-minute postoperative observation window. RESULTS: Postoperative stroke occurred in seven patients, six of whom were symptomatic prior to the procedure. In exploratory penalized regression analyses, higher postoperative MES counts (OR 1.02 per MES, 95% CI 1.01-1.04; p < 0.001) and an intraoperative burden of ≥ 10 MES (OR 6.06, 95% CI 1.40-34.78; p = 0.016) were associated with postoperative stroke. Symptomatic patients exhibited a significantly higher embolic burden (6.7 ± 13.3 vs. 2.2 ± 5.0, p = 0.004). CONCLUSION: Beyond its role in guiding selective shunting, transcranial Doppler monitors the occurrence of microembolization, which could serve as a potential indicator of perioperative stroke. In this exploratory analysis, both an intraoperative burden of 10 or more MES and sustained postoperative microembolization were associated with postoperative stroke. Given the low number of events, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before they can guide perioperative management.

METHODS: A total of 257 carotid endarterectomy procedures in 254 patients were analyzed (154 symptomatic, 103 asymptomatic). Neuromonitoring, combining transcranial Doppler ultrasonography and continuous electroencephalography, was utilized to evaluate cerebral perfusion and detect microembolic signals (MES).

title: Isolation and Culture of Primary Murine Aortic Smooth Muscle Cells for In vitro Studies Relevant to Vascular Remodeling and Aortic Aneurysm Biology.
abstract: Isolation and cultivation of primary aortic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) provide a valuable approach for investigating cellular mechanisms underlying vascular diseases, including aortic aneurysms. The present article describes a detailed and optimized protocol for the isolation and cultivation of murine aortic SMCs from thoracic and abdominal aortic segments. The current procedure includes careful aortic dissection, removal of surrounding tissue, and a two-step enzymatic digestion using collagenase, elastase, and soybean trypsin inhibitor, followed by mechanical dissociation and cell expansion under defined culture conditions. Particular emphasis is given on steps that improve cell yield, purity, and reproducibility, including adventitial removal and controlled digestion timing. Using this approach, the primary SMCs can be successfully isolated and expanded, exhibiting characteristic morphology and growth patterns. This protocol provides a reproducible and adaptable approach for generating primary aortic SMCs and serves as a platform for in vitro studies relevant to vascular remodeling and aortic aneurysm biology.

title: Post-transfer reassessment for endovascular treatment: factors associated with changes in EVT eligibility.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Repeat imaging after interhospital transfer for endovascular treatment (EVT) remains controversial because EVT eligibility may change during transfer, whereas routine repeat imaging may delay reperfusion. We investigated factors associated with complete recanalization and extensive infarct progression, and their implications for post-transfer reassessment. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 200 consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion transferred for EVT between 2016 and 2020 who underwent repeat non-contrast CT, CT angiography, and serial neurological assessment. Primary outcomes were complete recanalization on repeat CT angiography and extensive infarct progression (ASPECTS 0-3) precluding EVT. Factors associated with both outcomes were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. RESULTS: Changes affecting EVT eligibility occurred in 19 patients (9.5%), including complete recanalization in 10 (5.0%) and extensive infarct progression in 9 (4.5%). Intravenous thrombolysis was associated with complete recanalization (OR 4.87, 95% CI 1.08-46.25; P = 0.039), while greater neurological improvement showed a consistent direction of association (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.00-1.18; P = 0.059). Greater neurological deterioration (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.97; P = 0.018) and lower baseline CTA source-image ASPECTS (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.34-0.79; P = 0.001) were associated with extensive infarct progression. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in ten transferred patients experienced clinically meaningful changes affecting EVT eligibility. Neurological reassessment combined with baseline CTA source-image ASPECTS may help identify patients most likely to benefit from repeat imaging and supports a selective rather than routine repeat imaging strategy after interhospital transfer.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Repeat imaging after interhospital transfer for endovascular treatment (EVT) remains controversial because EVT eligibility may change during transfer, whereas routine repeat imaging may delay reperfusion. We investigated factors associated with complete recanalization and extensive infarct progression, and their implications for post-transfer reassessment. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 200 consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion transferred for EVT between 2016 and 2020 who underwent repeat non-contrast CT, CT angiography, and serial neurological assessment.

title: Apixaban vs rivaroxaban for venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants are first-line therapy for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet comparative evidence between apixaban and rivaroxaban remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in patients with VTE. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 2026. Studies directly comparing apixaban and rivaroxaban in adult VTE patients were included. Outcomes, including recurrent VTE, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, and net clinical harm, were pooled using a random-effects model. Thirteen studies comprising more than 220,000 patients were included. Apixaban was associated with a significantly lower risk of recurrent VTE compared to rivaroxaban (RR 0.85; 95% CI 0.74-0.98), with moderate heterogeneity. Apixaban was also associated with a significant 28% reduction in major bleeding risk (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with low heterogeneity, indicating consistent findings across studies. When efficacy and safety outcomes were combined, apixaban demonstrated a significantly lower risk of net clinical harm (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.68-0.86). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.80-1.12), with substantial heterogeneity across studies. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings, with no single study significantly altering the overall estimates. Overall, apixaban demonstrated a more favorable efficacy and safety profile compared with rivaroxaban in VTE management, with reduced recurrence and bleeding risk, while mortality remained comparable. These findings suggest that apixaban may be associated with a more favorable efficacy and safety profile than rivaroxaban; however, the results should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of observational evidence.

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in patients with VTE. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 2026.
